story_type: inflatable Mars decelerator ring tested on a rocket sled, high-speed camera
hook: A ring that has to inflate while hitting Mars faster than sound.
narration: This ring has to inflate around a spacecraft while it hits the air of another planet faster than sound.
Engineers at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory built it for future landers headed to Mars.
To test it here on Earth, they mounted it on a tower riding a rocket sled, in the desert at China Lake, California.
Mars air is so thin that a parachute alone struggles to slow a heavy lander. A wide inflated ring makes the spacecraft bigger, so it catches more of that thin air.
A high-speed camera filmed the whole inflation, slowed way down.
Watch the edge swell, ripple, and pull tight.
outcome: The ring filled all the way around the disk and held its shape as the rocket sled roared off down the track.
title: Mars brake ring inflated on a rocket sled
description:
In fall 2012, NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory filmed rocket sled testing of the SIAD-R, an inflatable supersonic decelerator built to slow spacecraft entering the atmosphere of another planet, at China Lake, California.

facts.claim: Built by the LDSD project at JPL as a supersonic deceleration device
facts.source_quote: The SIAD-R is one of three supersonic deceleration devices now being prepared for flight testing by the Low-Density Supersonic Decelerator project at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Pasadena, Calif.

facts.claim: Slows vehicles entering another planet's atmosphere, meant for Mars missions
facts.source_quote: The devices, which slow the rate of descent for vehicles entering the atmosphere of another planet, could be used in Mars missions launching as early as 2018.
